tools.name: compare_snapshots
tools.title: Compare snapshots
tools.description: What differs between two models, each working (the working model), a snapshot id (list_snapshots) or, in maquettiste mcp only, a folder that holds another copy of the project (compared without its packs): {from, to, added, removed, changed, kinds: [{kind, added, removed, changed}], packages: [{id, name, added, removed, changed}], elements: [{id, kind, name, change, path, previousName, previousPath, package, database, label, fields, fieldsTruncated}], next, files: [{path, change}], filesTruncated, packsCompared}. Elements are matched by id and compared by hash (a rename or a moved file says so); the other documents (settings, locale shards, extensions, rule and calculation files) by path. Elements are grouped by package: packages by qualified name, then (no package), then the migration facts of each database (database and label instead of package); a package's own row carries its parent; inside a group by kind, name and id. With fieldChanges each changed element lists its field changes (at most 50), each naming the sub-element it belongs to (subId, subKind, subName, subPointer: attribute code, /name), and limit defaults to 50. format markdown answers {markdown, next}: the page as maquettiste model diff --format markdown prints it, for a pull request or a change log. Pages by offset and limit (next is the next offset). With id, one element instead: its two documents (before, after) and the fields that differ as JSON pointers with their sub-element; with format markdown {markdown, next}, next always null. Compare with the snapshot taken before a change, then summarize by package.

from.description: working, a snapshot id or (maquettiste mcp only) a folder; required.

to.description: working (the default), a snapshot id or (maquettiste mcp only) a folder.

id.description: An element id: answer with that element's two documents and changed fields instead of the list.

offset.description: The first element of the page (default 0).

limit.description: The page size, 1 to 5000 (default 500, or 50 with fieldChanges or format markdown).

fieldChanges.description: List each changed element's field changes, each naming its sub-element (default false).

format.description: json (the default) or markdown: {markdown, next}, the review form of the page.

tools.name: get_binding_drift
tools.title: Binding drift
tools.description: What changed in each binding's source table since the binding's provenance was recorded, from files only (the model is never resolved): {bindings, next}, each binding {entity, entityName, binding, database, databaseName, source, sourceName, hasProvenance, stale, added: [{column, name, status}], renamed: [{column, name, attribute, attributeName}], retyped: [{column, name, attribute, attributeName}], removed: [column ids]}, ordered by entity name, entity id, database name, then database id. A binding records provenance when map-by-name, resync-binding or a materialize operation writes it; only a designed or imported table file has it. added lists the source's columns not recorded that nothing in the binding names, with what fills them (unaccounted, identity, default, computed); without provenance it lists only the unaccounted ones (MQ4047). renamed and retyped are mapped columns whose name or type changed since they were recorded (MQ4087); attributeName names a relation end's field <navigation>Id, its <endId>.type field <navigation>Type and its <endId>.<entityId> field <navigation><Entity>Id; a change of case or separators is not a rename. removed lists recorded ids the source no longer has. stale is provenance that does not describe the source (MQ4088), read as none. By default only bindings with something to report are listed; all lists every binding. Pass next as cursor until it is null. Catch up with apply_batch {"op":"resync-binding","database":...,"entities":[...]} after preview_materialize with the same op. An unknown database, entity or cursor is bad-request.

database.description: Only the bindings to this database, by id or name.

entities.description: Only the bindings of these entities, by id.

all.description: List every binding, also those with nothing to report (default false).

cursor.description: The next value of the previous page.

tools.name: get_calculated
tools.title: Calculated values
tools.description: The calculated values the project's calculation files (extensions/calculated/*.js) compute for the objects the ids name, evaluated for those objects and whatever they read, nothing else: {items: [{id, kind, holder, calculated}], missing, declarations, diagnostics}. One item per resolved object an id names; an attribute held by several entities (inherited, or added by a stereotype) gives one item per holder, with holder set to the holder's id. calculated maps each name the object's kind declares to its value; a value that fails (MQ5010 thrown or over a limit, MQ5011 not fitting its schema, MQ5013 a cycle) is left out and its diagnostic is in diagnostics. declarations lists what the calculation files declare for the items' kinds (name, kinds, schema, description); missing lists the ids that name nothing. A model with errors returns no items and the errors in diagnostics. get_resolved_model pages also carry calculated values for their records.

ids.description: Element or sub-element ids (an entity, an attribute, a table, ...), 1 to 100; required.

names.description: Only these calculated value names; default every name each object's kind declares.

tools.name: get_database_view
tools.title: Database view
tools.description: The resolved physical view of one database: tables (from the entities mapped to it, by its byConvention setting or by mapping elements, their relations and overlays) with columns (dbTypeId when a column uses a database type), keys, indexes and foreign keys, views, sequences, routines (parameters and result with native types), database types (nativeName, isCreated), SQL objects (phase, dependsOn) and queries (parameters, sources, the select list with types, the trees as written, collections with their keys, and the SQL for the database's dialect), as generation sees them. Each table, view, sequence, routine, database type, SQL object and query carries its own file's annotations (displayName, pluralName, description, stereotypes, tags, category, properties, generation); a synthesized table without an overlay has none but the stereotypes its schema and package defaults give it, with their default properties. Columns, keys, foreign keys and indexes a stereotype contributes follow the table's own, keyed <tableKey>.<memberId>, and carry memberOrigin (source stereotype, schema-default or package-default; stereotype; memberId; the facets the table redefined), which own members leave null: name such a member by that keyed id, and change it on the stereotype or with the table's redefines and excludes, never by copying it as an own column. relationStorage, only for a database that places a relation with an end of several types: per relation, relationId, relationName, mappingId, tables (the tables that hold its links), leftOut and notStored ({endId, entityId}) and gaps ({endId, kind, text}): what the database can't enforce (MQ4118), kind one of no-foreign-key, shared-table, id-only, type-check, count-check, one-to-one-unique, link-unique, per-type-duplicates or rows-not-told-apart, text the check or unique to copy in the database's dialect when the kind has one.

tools.name: get_element
tools.title: Get element
tools.description: One element: its canonical JSON document (json), its hash (pass it as expectedHash to save or delete), its path, the typed element and its Markdown sidecar text.

tools.name: get_elements
tools.title: Get elements
tools.description: Element documents in pages: {items: [{id, kind, path, hash, json}], next, missing}, json being the canonical document as get_element returns it. Select by ids, or by the index filters (kind, package, tag, category, stereotype, query; AND), or both; fields keeps only those top-level members of each json (id and kind are always kept), for example ["name", "attributes"]. Ordered by kind, name and id; pass next as cursor until it is null. A change between pages is fine: the next page starts after the last element read.

ids.description: Element or sub-element ids (a sub-element id reads the element that holds it), at most 1000; ids that match nothing are listed in missing.

kind.description: Only this kind, for example entity, relation, enum, process, routine, database-type, sql-object, query; custom for every custom element, custom:<type> for one custom kind.

package.description: Only elements directly in this package, by package id or package name.

query.description: Only elements whose name contains this text, ignoring case.

fields.description: The top-level members to keep in each document, for example ["name", "package", "attributes"]; id and kind are always kept. Omit for whole documents.

cursor.description: The next value of the previous page.

tools.name: get_ledger_ddl
tools.title: Migration ledger DDL
tools.description: The DDL of the migration ledger (contract version 1) of one PostgreSQL database: three tables in the schema migrations.ledgerSchema names (default migration_ledger), contract (one version row), applied_fact (one row per applied migration fact) and applied_object (one row per object whose identity the writer owns). The DDL is idempotent and holds no transaction control: a migrator runs it inside its own transaction before it writes its rows. The answer is {contractVersion, database (its name), dialect, schema, ddl, grant}: grant is the read grant for the grantRead role (usage on the schema, SELECT on the three tables), else null. Roles belong to environments, so the grant is printed, never generated. The engine never reads a ledger. No PostgreSQL database, an unknown or non-PostgreSQL database, several PostgreSQL databases and none named, or an empty grantRead is bad-request.

database.description: The PostgreSQL database, by name or id; optional when the model has only one.

grantRead.description: A role to print the read grant for; quoted unless it is a plain lower-case name.

tools.name: get_materialize_status
tools.title: Materialize status
tools.description: What can be materialized in one database: {database, databaseName, entities: [{id, name, package, projected, table}] (the entities with no binding to the database; projected says the database still projects a table for it by convention or a mapping element), sources: [{id, kind (table or view), name, schema, origin, boundBy: [{entity, entityName, binding, constants}]}] (its designed and imported tables and its views; boundBy empty means no entity is bound to it, several entries mean constant columns tell the entities apart)}. Then preview_materialize, and apply_batch with a materialize-tables, materialize-entities, materialize-attributes or materialize-columns operation.

tools.name: get_model_index
tools.title: Model index
tools.description: Summaries of the top-level elements (id, kind, name, package, tags, category, stereotypes, hash, path; operation rows add subject and effect, and verb when the operation names one; process rows add verbs, the verb keys their events, transitions and rights name, when they name any, and rights, the number of entries in a lifecycle's rights, when it has any; approvals and signatures, the number of its gates with stages and of their named signatures, each when above zero; named right rows add access and verbs; relation rows add ends, each with role and the entity of a one-type end, and for an end that writes types or anyEntity its entities (entity entries), stereotypes (ids), covers (the carriers of those stereotypes) and anyEntity, each only when present; custom element rows type and memberCount). Every filter is optional and they combine with AND. Without cursor or limit the answer is the whole list; with either it is one page, {items, next}, ordered by kind, name and id: pass next as cursor until it is null. Use the index to find elements, get_elements to read their documents in bulk, get_resolved_model for what generation sees (resolved types, inherited attributes, tables), get_model_kinds for the counts.

kind.description: Only this kind, for example entity, relation, enum, value-object, scalar-type, package, database, table, view, sequence, routine, database-type, sql-object, query, mapping, diagram; custom for every custom element, custom:<type> for one custom kind.

package.description: Only elements directly in this package, by package id or package name.

query.description: Only elements whose name contains this text, ignoring case.

cursor.description: The next value of the previous page; pages the answer.

limit.description: The page size, 1 to 1000 (100 when only a cursor is given); pages the answer.

tools.name: get_model_kinds
tools.title: Model kinds
tools.description: The kinds of top-level elements present with their counts ({total, kinds: [{kind, count}]}; custom elements count as one custom:<type> row per custom kind), and with by=package the same per package (packages: [{package, name, count, kinds}], the elements in no package first), so you know what to iterate before reading in bulk.

tools.name: get_plan
tools.title: Get plan
tools.description: A stored plan: its request, packs, every file with what apply does to it (added, modified, deleted; unchanged, not-rendered and kept are left alone; hand-edited, conflict, orphaned-owned), counts by kind, units by reason, and diagnostics (and, with units, every planned unit and output, each unit with the export values it declares, and the exports of the units the plan read without planning them).

planId.description: The plan id returned by plan; required.

tools.name: get_plan_diff
tools.title: Plan diff
tools.description: The unified diff of one file of a stored plan (the path as it appears in the plan's changes), without rendering again.

planId.description: The plan id returned by plan; required.

path.description: The repo-relative path of a file in the plan's changes, with / separators; required.

tools.name: get_project
tools.title: Project
tools.description: The project as a summary: name, the release running (productVersion, build) beside the engine contract (engineVersion) and the model format, the workspace (MAQUETTISTE_WORKSPACE, else the git branch, else the worktree name) with the branch and worktree, the settings hash, databases, packs ({name, version, description, units}), packDiagnosticCounts ({errors, warnings, info}), extensions (their names), customKinds (the type keys of the custom kinds the project declares in extensions/kinds/<type>.json) and sections, the sections you can ask for. Each section adds its full members: settings adds settings (the typed settings, also from get_settings), packs adds packManifests and packDiagnostics (also from list_packs), extensions adds extensionSchemas. Start here.

sections.description: The sections to add in full: settings, packs, extensions. Omit for the summary alone.

tools.name: get_references
tools.title: Where used
tools.description: Every reference to an element: the referring element id, the referring (sub-)element id, the JSON pointer and field in the referring document, and the referenced id. A custom property value an x-ref types is a reference too: its row carries schema (extension:<name> or stereotype:<key>) and, when every schema that types it allows remove-references to clear it, optional: true. A right refers to the actors in its actors and except, its own verbs, its states and ends and the paths of its condition; a lifecycle's use of a named right refers to it; a verb step refers to its end and object; a relation end's types entry refers to its entity or stereotype (/ends/1/types/0/entity).

tools.name: get_resolved_model
tools.title: Resolved model
tools.description: The resolved model, what templates read, as flat records in pages: {contract, schema, items, next, diagnostics, calculated}. contract is the contract version the page follows (until version 1, the version number of the Maquettiste release; it may change in any release) and schema names its JSON Schema, resolved-model.json: get_schema resolved-model:<scope> returns one scope's part (a project also holds it, with its reference resolved-model.md, in .maquettiste/.schema/v1/). Each record has id, kind and name; other objects appear by id. entities: attributes resolved (type, default, isKey, isInherited for the base's; an attribute without a description of its own shows the comment of the column a binding maps it to, and descriptionColumn names that column), key, alternate keys, base and derived, navigations (one to an end with several types has a null target and lists targets, that end's types), relations, mappings per database (table and columns), annotations, and revisions where the entity or a base has a revisions block: merged through the bases, with levels (number, name, format, values, first, skip, width, startEmpty, examples), separator, firstRevision, boundAttribute, and per governing lifecycle, attribute and relation end what a revise does (onRevise) and from, the entity that said it (null for the fallback). relations: ends, attributes, mappings; an end with several types (anyEntity, or types with two or more entries or a stereotype) has a null entity and adds types (entity ids, in order), hasSeveralTypes, stereotypes (ids), anyEntity and commonBase (the nearest entity every type is or derives from, when there is one), each left out on a one-type end; both ends may have several types. A relation mapping record adds, each left out when empty: links (for a relation with an end of several types whose mapping states storage, one per pair of targets: table and ends, each end with end, type, isHolder, columns, referencedTable, referencedColumns, foreignKey, typeColumn and codes), constants and attributes (a designed junctionTable's fixed-value columns and relation attribute columns), leftOut (covered entities not placed in the database), notStored (placed targets no pointer reaches, MQ4120) and typeCodes (entity and code for every entity a type column holds). A binding field that maps a relation end with several types adds holds (id, type or key) and keyOf (the entity of an <endId>.<entityId> field), and a binding adds discriminatorValue when it sets one. processes: every state, transition, event, guard, action, gate and invoke, actors by id; a gate with stages (an approval) adds stages, each with its named signatures (stage, signers, required, requiredActors, allowRepeatSigner, when typed at the approval site, notBy as verb keys and transition ids, and where set delegateTo, remindAfter, escalateAfter, escalateTo and reauthenticate), each stage's round when not 1 and its when, and allowSignerAcrossSignatures when true; a scenario step adds response (when not sign), signature, delegateTo and onBehalfOf, and its expect signatures and notices, each only where present; an event names its verb key, and a transition the verb of its move (its own, else its event's) and nextRevision, the revision level the move moves, each only where set. A lifecycle adds rightsDefault, as its file writes it, and rights, its entries in file order (an inline right with what it says, or a use of a named right, each with its states and its condition typed for the lifecycle), only where present. operations: subject, level, effect, verb (only where named), input members (type, keyOf or file with mediaTypes), outcomes (isDefault, completes, returns with members, entity or file, list, paging and maxPageSize), errors (code, input, and memberOrigin for an error a stereotype contributes, keyed <operationId>.<errorId>), defaultOutcome, fires and requires by id. custom-elements: one custom element per record with type, package, content as written and members (id, name, array, parent, pointer), every member at any depth. constraints: one named constraint per record with its typed parameters, condition and message; an entity's checks, a derived attribute's value and a process or operation guard's condition are written in the same expression language, each {text (printed from current names), type, nullable, tree (the ids the file holds)}, keys a model without expressions does not have. databases: the database view (tables with columns, keys, foreign keys and indexes, members a stereotype contributes keyed <tableKey>.<memberId> with their memberOrigin, and on a table without a file the stereotypes its schema and package defaults give it; views, sequences, routines, database types, SQL objects, queries with their SQL); tables, routines, database-types, sql-objects, queries: one object per record. migrations: one open migration fact per record, by database name then applied order, with its state, missing intent, after links, object, current key, from, to and content hash. Also packages, enums, value-objects, scalar-types, reference-types (with rows), seeds, actors, scenarios; all also lists one verb record per item of model.verbs (key, displayName, description, builtIn, group, hidden, used, and the ids of the events, transitions and operations that name it), only when the project uses verbs; all also lists one right record per named right (access, actors, except, verbs, ends, conditionText, and the lifecycles that use it), only when the model has named rights; a scenario step adds verb, values, end and object for a verb step, and its expect refusal and refusedBy, only where set; all is every scope but tables, routines, database-types, sql-objects and queries, which databases holds. Each page also carries calculated: the calculated values of its records and the sub-objects they list, by site (the object id, or <holder id>/<attribute id> for an attribute its holder does not own) then name; a value that fails is left out and its diagnostic joins diagnostics. A model with errors returns no items and the errors in diagnostics, unless its only errors are pending migration facts (MQ4101): those still return items.

scope.description: all (default), packages, entities, relations, enums, value-objects, scalar-types, reference-types, seeds, processes, actors, scenarios, operations, custom-elements, constraints, databases, tables, routines, database-types, sql-objects, queries or migrations.

database.description: A database id: only the entities and relations mapped to it, that database, its tables and its migration facts.

cursor.description: The next value of the previous page.

tools.name: get_rights
tools.title: Who can do what
tools.description: Who can do what in a lifecycle: per atomic state, actor and verb, whether the verb is allowed, denied or depends, read from the model without resolving it: {lifecycle, rightsDefault, rows: [{state, actor, verb, entity, answer, byDefault, by, dependsOn}], next}. The actors are those the lifecycle's rights (actors and except), events, human tasks and gates' signers name, by name, then everyone else (actor null); the verbs are those its rights and events name. A row is one kind of caller: one who satisfies that actor, and so every actor it is a member of, and no other actor the grid names. Each lifecycle answers on its own and any no wins: the lifecycle's denies, then its allows (an event that names the verb and can be sent from the state lets its actors through, a human task its actors for complete, a gate its signers for sign and for the gated event, an approval the signers of its named signatures for sign, reject, ignore, withdraw and the gated event, and for delegate where a signature has delegateTo), then its default; depends means a condition or an actor from the object decides. Another lifecycle that governs the object answers only for object, link and own verbs: one that says no in every one of its states denies the cell; one that could say no in only some of them, or under a condition, makes it depend and is named in dependsOn. When the lifecycle's subjects are governed by different other lifecycles and that changes a cell, the cell has one row per entity (entity); otherwise entity is left out. by names what decides: rights (an inline right, or the named right), events, human tasks, gates, or the lifecycle whose default answers (byDefault true). A project without rights still gets answers, from the closed lists and the default. Cells answer for a thawed object, where rights with whileFrozen hold nowhere; with frozen true they answer for a frozen object: modify, connect, disconnect and delete are denied by freezing before any right (answer denied, byDefault false, by empty, since no element decides it), and rights with whileFrozen hold. Rows come by state, actor, verb, then entity: pass next as cursor until it is null. A process that is no lifecycle, or an entity that is not one of its subjects, is bad-request. Nothing is written.

process.description: The lifecycle's id, name or model path; required.

states.description: State ids: only the rows of the atomic states that are, or are inside, one of them.

actors.description: Actor ids: only the rows of these actors (the row of everyone else is left out).

verbs.description: Verb keys: only the rows of these verbs.

entity.description: An entity id, one of the lifecycle's subjects: only the rows that hold for it.

frozen.description: True to answer for a frozen object: modify, connect, disconnect and delete are denied by freezing, and rights with whileFrozen hold. False or absent answers for a thawed object (default false).

cursor.description: The next value of the previous page.

tools.name: get_schema
tools.title: JSON schema
tools.description: The JSON schema (draft 2020-12) of an element kind or document, with the schema files it references (common.json) and, for an element kind, the project's extension schemas that apply to it (extensions: each constrains the element's properties object) and the typed parameters of the stereotypes that may apply to it (stereotypeParameters: [{stereotype, parameters}], each constraining the properties of the elements that carry the stereotype, implied ones included), so documents built for create_element, save_element, apply_batch or save_settings are valid. custom:<type> returns custom.json with customKind (the declaration with its path) and contentSchema (the compiled schema of content, with the id the engine owns on each member item). resolved-model returns the schema of get_resolved_model's pages (large: prefer resolved-model:<scope>, such as resolved-model:entities, which holds that scope's record and what it reaches), with contract, the version it describes. common.json lists the built-in verbs with their fixed meanings ($defs/builtInVerb); a project adds its own in verb-vocabulary (model/vocabularies/verbs.json) and names a verb by key in an event's, an eventless transition's or an operation's verb.

kind.description: An element kind (entity, relation, enum, value-object, scalar-type, package, database, table, view, sequence, routine, database-type, sql-object, query, mapping, diagram, stereotype, tag-vocabulary, category-tree, verb-vocabulary), custom:<type> for a custom kind the project declares, resolved-model or resolved-model:<scope> for the resolved model's pages, or a document (maquettiste for the settings, batch, pack, extension, custom-kind, declared-rules for a rule declaration file extensions/rules/<name>.json); required.

tools.name: get_settings
tools.title: Project settings
tools.description: The project settings (.maquettiste/maquettiste.json): the typed settings, the canonical JSON (json) and its hash for save_settings.

tools.name: get_trigger_sequence
tools.title: What happens when
tools.description: What runs, in order, when a verb happens in a lifecycle: the steps of the fixed order, read from the model without resolving it: {lifecycle, verb, steps: [{order, step, triggerPoint, lifecycle, type, timing, severity, states, targets, transitions, entities, attributes, ends, when, outside}]}. The built-in steps that apply come first (1 frozen, 2 closed-lists, 3 denies, 4 defaults, 5 no-move, 6 guards, 7 signatures), then the trigger points; at a transition whose gate has stages (an approval), reject, ignore and withdraw are answered too, as signature verbs, with the approval's checks (signers, denies on the response's verb, notBy, an earlier answer, nothing to withdraw, the reason) and the response's effect (a rejection clears the approval and moves nothing, an ignore finishes the person, a withdraw takes back a signature) as built-in steps, and so is delegate where a signature of the approval has delegateTo (the checks run on the person who delegates, then the person it goes to must be one of the delegateTo actors; the effect hands the signature over and moves nothing), while a gate without stages answers sign only: 8 before (actions that prepare the proposed values before the checks), 9 checks (an error refuses with refusal check and the check as refusedBy, a warning lets the step through and is listed in checkWarnings), 10 effect (the verb's built-in effect, or the replace that takes its place: only delete, disconnect, copy and revise allow one), 11 with-change (actions in the same unit of work, after the effect), 12 after-commit (actions once the change is saved; they may run late or more than once). A trigger point's step carries its id, the lifecycle whose list holds it, its type (check, action or replace), an action's timing (before, with-change or after-commit), a check's severity (error or warning), the places it is narrowed to (states, targets: the states a move enters, transitions, entities, attributes, ends), when: true when it runs only when its when condition holds, and outside: true when the team's code reaches outside systems; members that don't apply are left out. At each moment the asked lifecycle's points come first, then, for an object, link or own verb, every other lifecycle that governs the object, by name, each in its list's order; move, signature and task verbs run only the asked lifecycle's. A condition, a when and a set read the object as it will be through subject. and its values before the verb through old. (null on create). A place not given is left open, but a point narrowed by attributes or ends is listed without them only if it is a check, as a run fails closed. Named trigger points (trigger-point elements, whose subjects name entities and stereotypes) come first at each moment, the one whose subject is the farthest base first, then those an entity brings before those a stereotype brings, then by name; their steps carry subjects, exceptEntities and noBypass (never skipped by a bulk load) and no lifecycle. A named point on a move, signature or task verb runs only in the lifecycle whose move it is, never in an orchestration. With no entity given, a process with several subjects lists only the named points that cover every subject, and generated code runs only those. Given entity and no process, it answers for an object of that entity with no lifecycle acting, such as a customer's create: the named points that cover it, then every lifecycle that governs it, each reading every state; only object, link and own verbs (a move, signature or task verb is bad-request there), and state and transition are not read. A project without trigger points gets the built-in steps alone. One page, no cursor. A process that is no lifecycle, an unknown verb, or a state, entity or transition the lifecycle doesn't have is bad-request. Nothing is written.

process.description: The lifecycle's id, name or model path; required unless entity is given alone.

verb.description: The verb, by key (promote, modify, delete, sign, an own verb ...); required.

state.description: A state id of the lifecycle the object is in (for a move, its source); every state when absent.

entity.description: An entity id the lifecycle governs: only the points that run for it. Without process, the entity whose objects the verb happens to with no lifecycle acting.

attributes.description: Attribute ids the step reads or changes, for read and modify.

end.description: A relation end id of the subject, for a verb on a link.

transition.description: A transition id of the lifecycle, for a move verb or sign.

tools.name: list_migrations
tools.title: Migration facts
tools.description: The open migration facts (kind migration: one change stored rows must follow per file, recorded by writes), in applied order: by database name, then the order their after links give (ties by id). Each is {id, database, databaseName, order, fact (rename, rekey, change-type, drop, backfill, raw, adopt, baseline, value-map, state-map), state (pending, complete, held, released), stale, missing (the intent a pending fact lacks: conversion, dataCheck, acknowledge, value, skipWhen), summary, object (as recorded), after, path, hash}. stale marks a fact whose effect the model no longer shows (MQ4103): fold_migrations removes it. Complete a pending fact with save_element. The answer is one page, {facts, total, next}: pass next as cursor until it is null. An unknown database or cursor is bad-request.

database.description: Only this database's facts, by name or id.

cursor.description: The next value of the previous page.

tools.name: list_packs
tools.title: Template packs
tools.description: The template packs under .maquettiste/templates/ with their manifests (units, output roots, options, and uses: the packs each uses, with a version range), usedBy (pack name to the packs whose uses name it, then maquettiste.json when the project's uses does) and the diagnostics of loading them (MQ6042 to MQ6046 for uses problems and libraries nothing uses). A library pack has no units.

tools.name: list_snapshots
tools.title: Snapshots
tools.description: The model's snapshots (named copies of the whole model under .maquettiste/model-snapshots/), newest first: id, name, description, author, createdUtc, origin (user, or before-restore for the safety snapshot a restore takes), published, includesPacks, modelHash, files, elements and the count per kind. Compare one with the working model with compare_snapshots.

tools.name: list_validation_rules
tools.title: Validation rules
tools.description: The built-in validation rules. With no argument, a summary by family: {total, families: [{family, familyLabel, rules, first, last}]}, family being the hundreds group such as MQ72xx. With family, ids, query, cursor or limit, full entries in id order, one page {items, next}: each item is id, defaultSeverity, description, family, familyLabel, canBeOff (false for MQ1xxx) and quickFix (when the rule has one); the filters combine with AND; pass next as cursor until it is null. Override a rule's severity with validation.rules in the settings (get_settings, save_settings): error, warning, info or off.

family.description: Only the rules of this family, for example MQ41xx.

ids.description: Only these rule ids, matched exactly, for example ["MQ2001", "MQ4101"].

query.description: Only the rules whose id or description contains this text, ignoring case.

cursor.description: The next value of the previous page.

tools.name: localization_status
tools.title: Localization status
tools.description: The default locale, the declared locales and, per translated locale, its fallback chain and per shard the expected, translated, missing and stale counts (as GET /api/localization). The counts cover the standard fields, the texts of x-translatable custom properties (properties/<name>) and the x-translatable content texts of custom elements and their members (content/<name>).

tools.name: preview_binding_sql
tools.title: Preview binding SQL
tools.description: The SQL an entity's binding renders to, for its database's dialect or another: {preview: {entityId, bindingId, database, dialect, select, selectByKey, insert, update, delete}, diagnostics}, each statement {sql, parameters} or null when the binding does not have it (a read-only binding has no insert, update or delete). select reads every row (the constants filter it; a query source is wrapped as a derived table), selectByKey adds the key fields, insert writes the fields and constants without the columns the database fills and returns generated keys, update sets the updatable fields by key with the constants in the where clause, delete deletes by key or runs the soft-delete update. Parameters are named after the fields (@name, or : / $ with placeholder). preview is null when the model has errors.

dialect.description: postgresql, sqlserver, mysql, sqlite or oracle; omit for the binding's database's dialect.

tools.name: preview_expression
tools.title: Preview expression
tools.description: One expression of the expression language (a check, an entity check, a derived value, a process or operation guard, a value an action sets, a constraint's condition, a right's condition, a named signature's when), read from one element and never the whole model: {preview: {text, type, nullable, javascript, sql, sqlNote, answer}, diagnostics}. text is printed from current names; type is bool, int16, int32, int64, decimal, double, string, date, time, datetime, datetimeoffset, uuid, json, enum <id> or code <id>; javascript is the function over a row that calls the expression runtime as mq; sql is the PostgreSQL text through the one table the site reads (a table's own columns; for an entity's check or value, its binding's field map onto the binding's table), else null with sqlNote saying why (a guard or a constraint reads no table, another dialect is MQ4056). Preview a stored expression with element (the element, or the check, guard, attribute or set that holds it) and at (its pointer, /checks/0/condition, /actions/0/sets/0/value; optional when the element holds one), or text that is not saved with element, text and site: check, value or guard, or set with element the action and attribute the id of the attribute the value is for (its type must fit, MQ3103), or the pointer of a site, whose scope and mode the text takes (a JavaScript guard's /guards/0/condition reads the payloads of the events that use it; use it to rewrite a guard by hand and compare with simulate_process). values (a JSON object of the row by member name: a table's column names, an entity's attribute names, a process's context with the event's payload under event, an operation's input with the subject under subject) adds answer under the site's mode: a check passes on true or unknown, a guard holds on true only, a value answers itself (a decimal as exact text); now() reads the sandbox's fixed clock, 2000-01-01T00:00:00Z. current_actor() (who acts) and in_state(object, states) (whether an object is in a state of a lifecycle) preview at guard, set and right sites only, with no sql and no answer: only a simulation knows who acts and the states of a run. Send numbers with many digits as strings. preview is null when the text does not parse or the expression does not type (MQ3101 to MQ3113 in diagnostics). A right's condition previews at its pointer (/rights/0/condition on a lifecycle, /condition on a named right), or as text with site right; a named signature's when at its pointer (/transitions/1/gate/stages/0/signatures/0/when), needed unless false, and an approval stage's when at its pointer (/transitions/1/gate/stages/0/when), skipped when false; a named right with no use needs lifecycle. An unknown element is not-found; a request without element, with both at and text, an unknown site or database, is bad-request. Nothing is written.

element.description: The id of the element, or of the check, guard, derived attribute or set, that holds the expression, or on which text is written; for text at site set, the id of the action; required.

at.description: The pointer of a stored expression in the element's file (/checks/0/condition, /guards/1/condition, /attributes/3/derived/value) or of what holds it (/checks/0); omit when the element holds one, and with text.

text.description: Text to preview instead of a stored expression, for example issuedOn <= dueOn; needs site.

site.description: With text: check (a table, stereotype, entity or constraint), value (an entity's derived value), guard (a process or operation), set (a value the action element names sets, with attribute) or right (a right's condition, on a lifecycle or a named right), or the pointer of one of the element's sites.

attribute.description: With site set: the id of the attribute the value is for, whose type the value must fit (MQ3103).

database.description: A database id or name: an entity's expression lowers to SQL through its binding to that database; omit for the binding that lists the check, or the only one.

lifecycle.description: A lifecycle id or name: a named right's condition, or text written for one, previews as if the right were used there. Without it a named right's condition previews in the scope of all its uses; a named right with no use needs one.

values.description: The row the expression reads, members by name; adds answer.

tools.name: preview_materialize
tools.title: Preview materialize
tools.description: What a materialize or binding operation would do, without writing: {operation, database, valid, creates, updates, deletes (each {id, kind, name, path, because, element}: element is the document that would be written), notes, diagnostics}. op materialize-tables with entities (and an optional schema id) writes, per entity, a designed table with exactly the shape its projection has (columns, keys, uniques, checks, indexes, foreign keys, comments; its overlay folds into the table, which keeps the overlay's id), binds the entity to it, deletes its mapping to the database and points relation mappings at the foreign keys; op materialize-entities with tables (designed or imported tables and views) and package writes, per table, an entity (one attribute per column, the key from the primary key) bound to it, and a many-to-one relation per foreign key between them; op materialize-attributes with entities (each bound to the database) and, for one entity, optional columns (keys or physical names) adds, per entity, an attribute per column of its binding's source (the columns named, else every column nothing in the binding names: unaccounted, identity, a default), named and typed from the column and mapped to it in the binding; op materialize-columns with entities (each bound to the database, reading a designed or imported table it writes) and, for one entity, optional attributes (binding field references: attribute ids, attributeId.memberId, to-one end ids) adds a column of that table per attribute the binding leaves unmapped, shaped as the entity's projection would make it (the project's naming and type conventions), mapped to it; a column whose name the table has is left out with a note, and no foreign key is added. op map-by-name with entities (each bound to the database) maps every attribute the binding leaves unmapped to a free column of the same loose name (case and every character but letters and digits ignored; an attribute's name, attributeMember for a value object member, a to-one navigation's name plus Id), writing column ids for a table file and names for a view, and records provenance for a table file; op resync-binding with entities (each bound to a table file), optional columns (one entity: keys or physical names) and keepNames brings each binding into step with its table in one batch: an attribute that followed its column's old name takes the new one (keepNames keeps every name), a retyped column retypes its attribute unless its reference type, enum or scalar type still fits, unmapped attributes map by name, an attribute is added per added column, fields of removed columns are removed (attributes stay), and provenance is recorded again; attribute ids never change. Both are refused (MQ4089) for an entity with no binding to the database, a source they cannot read, misused columns, or nothing to map or re-sync. They read files only, and their diagnostics come from resolving the named database alone. An entity already bound, or a table an entity is bound to, is refused (MQ4055), as is an entity with no binding to the database, a query source or a column already mapped (materialize-attributes), or a source that is not a table file or an attribute already mapped (materialize-columns). Apply it with apply_batch: {"op":"materialize-tables","database":...,"entities":[...]}, {"op":"materialize-entities","database":...,"tables":[...],"package":...}, {"op":"materialize-attributes","database":...,"entities":[...],"columns":[...]}, {"op":"materialize-columns","database":...,"entities":[...],"attributes":[...]}, {"op":"map-by-name","database":...,"entities":[...]} or {"op":"resync-binding","database":...,"entities":[...],"keepNames":true}.

op.description: materialize-tables, materialize-entities, materialize-attributes, materialize-columns, map-by-name or resync-binding; required.

entities.description: The entity ids (materialize-tables, materialize-attributes, materialize-columns, map-by-name, resync-binding).

schema.description: The schema id of the database the tables go to (materialize-tables); omit to keep each projected table's schema.

package.description: The package id the entities go to (materialize-entities).

columns.description: The source columns, as keys or physical names (one entity): those that get an attribute (materialize-attributes; omit for every column nothing in the binding names), or those to bring into step (resync-binding; omit for every column of the source).

attributes.description: The binding field references (attribute ids, attributeId.memberId, to-one end ids) that get a column (materialize-columns, one entity); omit for every attribute the binding leaves unmapped.

keepNames.description: Keep every attribute's name, even one that followed its column's renamed name (resync-binding; default false).

tools.name: preview_query_sql
tools.title: Preview query SQL
tools.description: The SQL a query renders to, for its database's dialect or another: {preview: {id, name, database, dialect, sql, parameters, collections: [{name, sql, parameters, keys}]}, diagnostics}. sql uses @name placeholders (placeholder : or $ for :name or $1, $2...); a list parameter is written IN @name, for a data access library that expands lists (lists any writes = ANY(@name) on PostgreSQL). Each collection is a second statement run once for all parent rows: it takes the parent rows' key values as the list parameter mq_keys0 (mq_keys1...) and returns each row's key as mq_key0, which matches the parent row's keys[i].parentField. preview is null when the model has errors (they are in diagnostics); an sql expression without a text for the dialect is MQ4029.

dialect.description: postgresql, sqlserver, mysql, sqlite or oracle; omit for the query's database's dialect.

lists.description: How list parameters are written: expand (default) or any.

tools.name: preview_seed_rows
tools.title: Preview seed rows
tools.description: One seed's rows, one page at a time, never the whole model's: {seed, script, database, rows: [{id, key, values, refs}], total, next, diagnostics}. Without database, the rows as the seed writes them (inline or in its CSV rows file) or as its rows script (rowsFrom.script, extensions/seeds/*.js) returns them: values by the seed's column names, as written; key is the row key in seed terms (a reference type's code, a table seed's key columns, a foreign-key entry's natural key), empty when the target has none; a scripted row's id derives from the seed and its key, so it is the same on every call. With database (an id or name), the rows that database receives from the seed, in database terms: values by the table's column names with stable ids and the values foreign-key entries fill, key the row key there (null where the database fills a part), and refs: per foreign-key entry {foreignKey, table, key, found, unknown}, found false when no row has the natural key (MQ7111), unknown the columns whose referenced value the database fills (a pack looks them up). Only the seed's script and the scripts of the seeds its foreign-key entries name run. diagnostics holds the script's findings (MQ7116, MQ7127, MQ7128, MQ5005) or, with database, the errors that keep the model from resolving (no rows then). Pass next as cursor until it is null. An unknown seed is not-found; an unknown database or cursor is bad-request.

database.description: A database id or name: gives the rows in that database's terms; omit for the rows as written.

cursor.description: The next value of the previous page.

tools.name: preview_unit
tools.title: Preview unit
tools.description: Renders one unit of a pack for one element with no writes and returns each file's output path and text, the diagnostics and the keys the render read. A copy unit lists every file it copies: a text file with its output text, a binary file with binary true and empty text; a source pattern matching nothing fails it with MQ6030. overlay (pack-relative path to unsaved text), unitOverride (an unsaved unit with the same id) and parameters render unsaved work; a disabled pack previews too. A render that does not finish within 4 x limits.scriptTimeoutMs (8000 ms when it is 0, the wall clock off for scripts) fails with MQ6007. An element outside the unit's scope (none for an each unit, another kind, one a selector does not return, any for a model unit) renders nothing and returns MQ6026, which names the kind the template expects. A unit whose one render covers the whole model (for: model), a database or a locale renders all of it: preview it when its output is what you need.

elementId.description: The element id (or a resolved table key); omit for a model unit.

overlay.description: Pack-relative path to unsaved text of templates, partials and scripts.

unitOverride.description: An unsaved unit object (as in pack.json units) used instead of the saved one; its id must equal unit.

parameters.description: Effective parameter values used instead of the defaults and project values.

tools.name: reference_type_usage
tools.title: Reference type usage
tools.description: Every attribute typed by a reference type: attribute, owner, domain (the owner's package), collection, required and the effective storage choice per database; and in columns, every designed, imported, extra and inherited column whose typeRef names it: table, column (a keyed id when inherited), database, domain (the table's package), required, the effective storage choice there and the bound table.

tools.name: tag_usage
tools.title: Tag usage
tools.description: The tags one tag vocabulary governs, as a summary: {package, vocabulary, strict, tags: [{tag, declared, uses, examples}], next}: every tag the vocabulary of package (the global one without it) declares, and every tag used inside that scope that no vocabulary on the element's domain chain declares, in key order, with its uses there (the element's own tags and its sub-elements') and up to five names of the elements holding it. The whole list unless limit or cursor pages it. With tag: {package, tag, declared, uses, elements, next}, the ids of the elements holding that tag in pages, in id order; a tag the scope neither declares nor uses is not-found. Pass next as cursor until it is null. A domain that declares the same key keeps its own uses. Remove tags everywhere, or rename one, with apply_batch {"op":"retag","tags":[...],"name":<new key, optional>,"package":<domain, optional>}.

package.description: The domain whose tag vocabulary it is; omit for the global one.

tag.description: One tag key: answers the ids of the elements holding it, in pages.

cursor.description: The next value of the previous page; pages the answer.

limit.description: The page size, 1 to 1000 (100 when only a cursor is given; always paged with tag); pages the answer.

tools.name: validate
tools.title: Validate
tools.description: Validates the whole model, or only some elements, with the built-in rules and, by default, the project's script rules (extensions/rules/*.js, findings x/<id>; a rule file that does not load is MQ5002 on that file) and declared rules (extensions/rules/*.json, findings x/<id>; MQ5014 to MQ5017 on the declaration files). On a model without errors it also evaluates every calculated value (extensions/calculated/*.js; MQ5010 to MQ5013 for the values that fail) and runs the rules registered with scope "resolved" on each resolved object of their kinds; validating some elements reports only what falls on them. Returns the diagnostics (rule id such as MQ3001, severity, message, element id, file path, JSON pointer, line and column) and the error, warning and info counts, and suppressed: the findings an element's suppressions accepted (its suppressions entries: rule, optional member, reason), each with the finding, the reason, the element and the entry's pointer (/suppressions/<i>), not counted. A whole-model validate whose model resolves warns MQ5020 for an entry that matched nothing. With against (a model snapshot id; a folder holding another copy of the project too, from the command-line server), the whole model is also compared with that baseline: a change since it that a migration must follow and no migration fact the baseline lacks explains is MQ4102, a fact whose combined effect the model no longer shows is MQ4103, baseline objects whose owners have errors are skipped with MQ4109. A value that names nothing is bad-request.

against.description: A model snapshot id (list_snapshots), or, where the server allows folders, a folder holding another copy of the project (relative to the server's current directory): compare the whole model with it. Leave elementIds out.

elementIds.description: Only these element ids (and, by default, the elements that reference them); omit for the whole model.

includeReferrers.description: Whether to include the elements that reference the scope (default true).

includeScriptRules.description: Whether to run the project's JavaScript rules (default true).
